findings.title: Failure disposition can abandon a still-live direct runner without a bounded reap
findings.trigger: An early independent snapshot, receipt write or wait fails after Popen succeeds while the runner remains live.
findings.evidence: The except block invokes runner.terminate() and immediately enters finally. Finally calls poll() for its recorded child list but performs no wait/communicate for this runner. The main function then returns. In contrast, the normal path waits at line 391 and snapshot timeout handling attempts a bounded wait at lines 167–172.
findings.consequence: FAILED_OR_UNKNOWN_HELD prevents false fixture acceptance, but the controller can exit while the directly owned runner is still processing TERM/cleanup and before it is reaped. The existing runner signal handler converts TERM to Failed and starts its cleanup path, so this is not a claim that TERM necessarily kills its cleanup. The controller nevertheless drops its retained handle and opportunity to observe/reap completion while budget may remain. This weakens the stated handle-through-disposition contract and leaves cleanup evidence incomplete on ordinary controller failures.
findings.requested_change: After requesting runner termination, retain and wait/reap that Popen handle using only the original controller hard-end time remaining. Record termination errors, timeout and reap outcome explicitly. A timeout must remain FAILED_OR_UNKNOWN_HELD, with no numeric-PID/group rescue, retry, extra guard or extended deadline. Preserve the independent scoped-cleanup requirement when observation is unavailable.
